about: A developer asks OpenCode to write Claude Code plugins for this repository, one step per prompt. The files it writes are throwaway: they live in a sandbox copy that is deleted after scoring and are never part of this repository's implementation.

turns.prompt: I am new to this repository. Give me a short overview (under 200 words): what it is, its main folders, and which agent hosts it already supports.
Look at how the Hermes plugin packages are laid out under hermes-plugins/. For hermes-relevance-filter, list its files and what each one is for, one line each.
Now read hermes-plugins/CONTRACT.md and summarize in at most 8 bullets what a host-specific package has to get right. Include the file and line where the host calls select_context.
Now read the OpenCode plugin (.opencode/plugins/context-engineering.ts and .opencode/README.md). List the hooks and tools it registers and what each one is for.
Look at context-core/src/context_core (runtime.py and the package __init__.py). Which classes and functions would a new host adapter call? Give each with a one-line purpose.

Skim docs/design/design.md and the three practice designs (relevance filtering, progressive tool disclosure, context graph). For each practice give me one sentence on what it does and one on what it needs from a host.

Claude Code plugins are directories with a .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest and optional hooks/hooks.json, hook scripts, skills, commands and an .mcp.json. Propose a layout under a new folder claude-code-plugins/ that mirrors hermes-plugins/: one package per practice (claude-code-relevance-filter, claude-code-progressive-tool-disclosure, claude-code-context-graph), a claude-code-all-three package, and claude-code-plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json. List the paths with one line each. Do not create any file yet.

Create claude-code-plugins/claude-code-relevance-filter with: .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json registering a PostToolUse hook, hooks/relevance_filter.py (reads the hook JSON from stdin, shortens tool results above a token threshold to the passages relevant to the latest user prompt using context_core, and prints the hook JSON output), README.md and tests/test_relevance_filter.py. Keep every file small (under about 80 lines) and use two or three tests. Then run the tests with python3.13 -m pytest and fix any failure.

Create claude-code-plugins/claude-code-progressive-tool-disclosure in the same style: .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/tool_disclosure.py (keeps the tool catalog small by showing tool names first and details on demand), README.md and tests/test_tool_disclosure.py. Then run its tests and fix any failure.

Create claude-code-plugins/claude-code-context-graph in the same style, with hooks/context_graph.py. Claude Code hooks cannot rewrite earlier messages, so implement what a hook can do (for example record each closed turn as a compact card in a local JSONL file and inject a short summary of earlier cards on UserPromptSubmit) and state that limitation in the README. Include .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json and tests/test_context_graph.py. Then run its tests and fix any failure.

Create claude-code-plugins/claude-code-all-three, one plugin that combines the three hook scripts under a single hooks/hooks.json (with its own .claude-plugin/plugin.json and README.md), and write claude-code-plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json listing the four packages.

Validate everything you created: run python3.13 -m py_compile on every Python file, python3.13 -m json.tool on every JSON file, and the full test suite under claude-code-plugins/ with python3.13 -m pytest. Report the counts and fix what fails.

Quick check from what you read earlier, without opening files again unless you must: which Hermes package has to be used to run all three practices together, and what exactly stops three separate plugins from being active at once?
And in the OpenCode plugin: how often, in milliseconds, does it send a heartbeat to the bridge, and why is that interval needed?
Add a short section about the Claude Code plugins to the top-level README.md with a table of the four packages and one line on how to install one.
Summarize what you built: every file you created, one line each, and anything you are unsure about or left unfinished.
